measurement: 20 ledgered decode tokens after 40 warmup, sealed Math-Preserve artifact, verify_hash on, GPU timestamps present on every token

quality_of_the_ledger.note: The gate forbade an unexplained orchestration bucket. There is none: 99.98 percent attributed with a 0.5 ms named remainder.

corrections_to_the_controller.cause: I counted matvec call SITES in source and multiplied by 78 layers. The real path does not execute every site every layer, and some sites share a command buffer. A static count is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

corrections_to_the_controller.claimed: ~1,171 pipeline drains at ~5.5 ms each explains ESSENTIALLY ALL of the token time
corrections_to_the_controller.measured: metal_synchronize_cpu_wait is 550.1 ms of 2,404.8 ms -- 22.9 percent, not ~100 percent
corrections_to_the_controller.why_it_matters: This was the most consequential wrong claim of the session. Acting on it would have sent the entire runtime effort at command-buffer collapse -- a 23 percent bucket -- while ignoring a 26 percent bucket I had explicitly deprioritized.

corrections_to_the_controller.claimed: lm_head may remain host dense for now; it runs once per token, not once per layer
corrections_to_the_controller.measured: final_head_and_sampling is 631.0 ms, 26.2 percent -- the SECOND largest bucket
corrections_to_the_controller.cause: Reasoned from frequency (once per token) and ignored magnitude (a dense 154,880-row vocabulary projection on the host). Frequency without size is not a cost argument.

new_finding_not_previously_suspected.what: active_bytes_read is 10.46 GB per token against a geometry requirement of 2.58 GB -- 4.05x more traffic than the routed-expert math needs.
new_finding_not_previously_suspected.why_it_matters: This is a bandwidth finding independent of synchronization. At 800 GB/s, 10.46 GB is 13 ms of unavoidable memory time versus 3.2 ms if only the required bytes moved. Even a perfect zero-overhead runtime would be 4x slower than the roofline suggests until this is explained.
candidate_causes_to_test: reading whole shards or pages rather than the exact tensor extents
the dense lm_head pulling a 154,880-row vocabulary matrix every token
codebooks re-read per expert rather than shared
mmap page-fault granularity exceeding payload size

reprioritized_work_order_by_measured_sha.action: Move the dense lm_head and sampling to device. Highest measured share with the clearest mechanism -- a host dense projection over 154,880 rows every token.
Explain and remove the 7.9 GB/token of traffic the geometry does not require. This gates every bandwidth-bound target below TG20.
Largest single bucket, but it is real expert compute. Attack it via the overread first, then fused multi-projection waves.
Still worth 23 percent and still requires GPU-resident state first. Demoted from 'the whole problem' to 'one of three comparable problems'.
Host Rust loops; moves with the GPU-resident-state lane.

what_the_ledger_settles: The runtime is not dominated by any single pathology. Three buckets of comparable size -- expert compute at 29.7 percent, host head and sampling at 26.2 percent, and synchronization at 22.9 percent -- account for 79 percent of the token. There is no single fix that reaches TG20; the collapse ladder has to attack all three.
not_evidence_of: that any of these buckets is reducible by a specific amount -- this says where the time is, not that it can be removed
